transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-24
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Head of ML, Concordia AI), Jenna Ortiz (VP Eng), Marcus Li (Infra Lead), Hannah Cruz (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed capacity uplift and sovereign edge onboarding; agreed to run benchmarks and deliver security docs; tentative extension of contract for 12 months with EU activation in early Nov.

[00:00] Alex Rivera: hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about an hour, uh plan to run through the q4 uplift numbers, eu sovereign edge ask and then next steps, priya is going to cover the bench plan and infra bits
[00:14] Priya Nair: hi all, thanks. quick agenda, sizing overview, region options (frankfurt vs ams), private vpc model, kms and audit logs, bench approach and sample sla targets
[00:28] Samir Patel: sounds good. to kick off, we are seeing a 2.3x on peak token throughput month over month, the product team wants more headroom for q4 marketing bursts. also we need eu data residency for a subset of traffic — full sovereign tenancy ideally
[00:45] Jenna Ortiz: and procurement is asking if we can lock in pricing for a 12 month extension with uplift tiers so we don't get surprised by month to month usage spikes
[01:03] Alex Rivera: right, so we mapped three uplift tiers: baseline +20% (small), +60% (expected), and +120% (burst). pricing model can be reserved capacity credits with burst pools — we can show committed discounts on reserved and a capped overage rate
[01:26] Marcus Li: on the eu sovereign edge, our security team wants the control plane outside of Redwood's shared infra — i.e., private control plane + customer VPC peering, and key management integration via our KMS HSM provider. is that supported?
[01:45] Priya Nair: yes, concordia on Private supports customer-managed control plane and vpc peering. for KMS we have integrations documented — we support bring-your-own-kms with envelope encryption. small caveat: some older model variants require extra kernel path testing for quantized runs on certain GPUs
[02:07] Samir Patel: when you say older model variants do you mean the 7b q4 quantized ones? we tried to run gptx-7q and saw crazy memory blowups last month in staging, so want to avoid surprises
[02:22] Priya Nair: exactly — certain 7b models with per-layer quant plugs need a different nv kernel. we'll run a compatibility pass during the bench window. if needed we fallback to a compatible variant with minor perf delta
[02:40] Jenna Ortiz: procurement question — for private deployment is there an additional licence or platform fee separate from reserved capacity? also SLA differences?
[02:56] Alex Rivera: yes there's a platform fee for Private deployments (one-time or annual), and we include an SLA for uptime and latency tiers as part of Dedicated/Private. we'll put those line items in the SOW; term pricing for 12 months will show committed vs burst rates
[03:17] Hannah Cruz: and auditability — we need immutable audit logs and ability to export to our SIEM. also SOC2 plus any ISO attestation docs would help our security review
[03:31] Priya Nair: we can provide audit logs exports, syslog / s3 sinks and retain per-route traces for the retention window. SOC2 Type II report and ISO certificate are in the security pack we'll send. there might be a small delay for extended retention beyond default
[03:48] Samir Patel: perfect. on the bench, priya, can you outline the metrics you will collect? we need tail-latency p95/p99, tokens/sec cost breakdown, and warm cache vs cold start numbers
[04:03] Priya Nair: yes we'll collect p50/p95/p99, per-token cost, kv cache hit ratio, gpu utilization, and end-to-end latency including network hop. we'll run A/B: hosted baseline vs private eu-edge, same model and prompt sets you gave us
[04:25] Marcus Li: about networking — do you support VPC peering or do you use transit gateway? our preference is peer to a transit gateway for the hub model
[04:36] Priya Nair: we support both peering and TGW. for multi-account setups TGW generally simplifies routing, but peering can be lower latency in single-account setups
[04:50] Jenna Ortiz: any competitors we should be aware of? our SRE evaluated AICore, but they lacked private control plane features; BigCompute had better burst pricing but weaker audits
[05:03] Alex Rivera: yep heard the same. we'll send a side-by-side on features and pricing notes in the SOW appendix
[05:17] Samir Patel: timeline wise, what does it look like from Redwood side to turn on EU sovereign edge once we sign?
[05:25] Alex Rivera: typical lead time is 3-4 weeks for private control plane + vpc config + cert provisioning, bench window can start earlier in a read-only staging mode. if we do a reserved commit it can accelerate provisioning
[05:41] Hannah Cruz: procurement needs a legal contact and a skeleton SOW to begin redlines. can you include termination clauses and data residency clauses explicitly?
[05:53] Alex Rivera: yes, we'll include termination, data residency, and breach remediations. legal will be on copy, I'll add Redwood legal contact in the doc
[06:07] Priya Nair: for the bench, do you have preferred prompts and token distribution? the earlier sample you sent looked skewed to very long form generation
[06:19] Samir Patel: we updated that file after last run. we'll share two datasets: conversational 16-64 tokens and long-form 300-1k tokens. Marcus will add a synthetic burst trace pattern too
[06:33] Marcus Li: yep I'll drop the traces in the staging bucket and share access. note that our infra team wants a 4 hour warm-up window before measuring, to get cache primed
[06:47] Priya Nair: makes sense. we'll do warm-up, three 1-hour runs, and a cold-start spike test between runs
[07:00] Jenna Ortiz: can you confirm pricing for the three tiers you mentioned? we need numbers to run through finance
[07:08] Alex Rivera: yes i'll include a committed tiered pricing table in the SOW: baseline, expected, burst. committed discounts scale with reserved capacity term length; will include both 12 and 24 month options
[07:24] Samir Patel: one more compliance note, some of our EU customers require 'customer-keyed encryption' meaning keys never leave our HSM. is BYOK compatible with that model?
[07:38] Priya Nair: BYOK with HSM is supported; we offer an envelope approach so your HSM keeps root keys, we manage ephemeral keys for the runtime but never see your root. we'll document the KMS flow and the attestation steps
[07:54] Hannah Cruz: perfect. procurement also asked about invoicing cadence and whether we can do quarterly invoices rather than monthly
[08:02] Alex Rivera: we can offer quarterly invoicing for committed contracts; we'll note that in the commercial terms in the SOW
[08:12] Samir Patel: ok great. let's talk lift numbers — we're targetting 300% peak capacity over current baseline for black-friday style bursts, but average still around 1.5x. do you have sizing guidance?
[08:27] Priya Nair: we'll map average qps to GPU instance types; for that profile we recommend a mix of dedicated pools and burstable shared capacity. we'll include recommended pool sizes per tier in the SOW and cost delta estimates
[08:44] Marcus Li: what's the rollback plan if we hit perf regressions after cutover? can traffic be routed back to hosted quickly?
[08:55] Alex Rivera: yes smart routing supports immediate fallback to hosted variants by policy. we can configure canary rollouts and automatic rollback thresholds (error rate, latency) — all tunable
[09:09] Jenna Ortiz: thanks. anything else on legal or security?
[09:14] Hannah Cruz: just to reiterate export controls — ensure that any model weights we host in eu remain within eu boundaries and that logs don't include PII in transit logs
[09:24] Priya Nair: agreed. we can enable PII redaction pre-ingest and ensure data at rest in eu regions only; we'll show config options in security pack
[09:36] Alex Rivera: ok wrapping up, i'll summarize the commitments: Redwood to deliver SOW + pricing + security pack by friday (2025-09-26), provision bench window pending staging access, and run A/B benches with metrics and a readout. Concordia to provide staging access, traffic shape and internal sign-off dates
[09:57] Samir Patel: yep will do, thanks all
[10:02] Jenna Ortiz: thanks everyone
[10:05] Marcus Li: thanks
[10:10] Hannah Cruz: thanks
